Although I had seen multiple reports on social media about these products causing significant breakouts, I believed that might not be my experience.

The reaction was so intense that I have had to continuously wear pimple patches, and I even experienced breakouts on my neck and jaw—areas where I have never had acne before.

Author: yruri
Title: Causes Foundation Separation Over Time
ReviewText:
Unfortunately, this did not meet my expectations.

The first issue for me was the scent. It has a distinctly chalky smell that makes the application experience unpleasant. For a product positioned as a refined skincare step, the fragrance feels distracting rather than soothing.

The texture is also extremely slippery, almost serum-like. While this may work well under skin tints or very lightweight bases, it does not perform well under long-wear foundations. I typically use Estée Lauder Double Wear, and although the base looks nice immediately after application, the performance does not last.

After a few hours of wear, the foundation begins to separate and break down, settling unevenly rather than wearing gracefully. Instead of extending wear time, this product seemed to compromise the longevity of my makeup.

Overall, this may suit those who prefer minimal makeup or tints, but for anyone relying on long-lasting, full-coverage foundations, this was disappointing and not something I would repurchase.

Author: Sylviacongcong
Title: makes the rest of my routine work better
ReviewText:
I’ve been testing the Rhode Glazing Milk Ceramide Facial Essence for the past couple of weeks, and I’m genuinely surprised by how quickly it worked its way into my daily routine. I tend to be pretty picky with essences because many of them feel either too watery to make a difference or too sticky to layer under makeup. This one actually sits right in the middle — the texture is milky and fluid, but it doesn’t leave any film or tackiness behind. It absorbs almost immediately, which makes it an easy first step after cleansing.

The biggest change I’ve noticed is the way it softens my skin right after application. My face tends to get a little flushed after washing, especially in the mornings, and this tones that down within a minute or two. It doesn’t “erase” redness overnight, but it definitely helps the skin settle faster. On days when my moisture barrier feels a bit compromised or I’ve over-exfoliated, this has been the one product that doesn’t sting at all — instead, it feels cooling in a subtle, comforting way.

Hydration-wise, it doesn’t give a heavy glow on its own, but it creates a nice, plump base for anything that comes after. When I layer moisturizer or sunscreen on top, they seem to sit more evenly, and my foundation blends noticeably smoother. I tried mixing a few drops into my foundation like the brand suggested, and it did give a softer, more skin-like finish without making my T-zone greasy.

I had them switch to double cleansing and wearing a proper amount of sunscreen. Suddenly, no more breakouts! I'm a huge fan of double cleansing and using at least two fingers worth of SPF for your face (as you should be per the American Academy of Dermatology). Using this product made my skin much healthier and glowy. I say this as someone with PCOS, rosacea, and sensitive skin who uses both retinoids and salicylic acid daily. So if you're finding it's breaking you out, please try double cleansing and proper SPF on your face.

Author: shellbeee
Title: Pretty packaging, harsh results.
ReviewText:
I really wanted to love this product because of all the hype and the gorgeous branding, but honestly, my skin had the worst reaction to it. Within just a couple of days of using it, I broke out so badly all over my cheeks and chin—it was like my skin was angry at me. I kept hoping it was just “purging” and tried to push through for another week, but the breakouts just got worse, painful, and left marks behind that I’m still dealing with.

I don’t normally have super sensitive skin, and I’ve used plenty of other hydrating products before without issues. But something in this formula just did not agree with me at all. It felt nice going on, I’ll give it that—it’s lightweight and gives that dewy look at first. But the aftermath was definitely not worth it.

For the price point and hype, I expected something gentle, effective, and worth adding to my routine. Instead, it set my skin back weeks. I’ve now had to strip back my skincare routine to heal from the breakouts this caused.

I know it works for some people, but if you’re acne-prone or even slightly sensitive, I would be very cautious. Definitely not worth the hype in my experience, and I wouldn’t repurchase.

Title: real review in midst of fake reviews/perioral derm
ReviewText:
I was very confused to see what seems to be hundreds of negative reviews that are not verified, or provide no photo or proof that they even own the product, and most seem to be accounts that have just been created on Sephora's website. 

As background, I am in my mid-30s and I have a skin condition called perioral dermatitis. It's like a combination of eczema, rosacea and acne. I have to be extremely careful with what skincare I put on my face because my skin is extremely reactive. I have gone through four bottles of this product. I am always sketpical to try something new but combing through the ingredients (having a skincare condition will make you very vigilant and knowledgable on skincare ingredients) - ceramides, beta-clucan, copper, magnesium, zinc, cholesterol are all great for my inflammatory skin condition. Rhode's cosmetic chemist Ron Robinson is a genius and every product he's made in his career is a slam dunk for sensitive skin. He's worked at Estee Lauder, Clinique, La Mer and has his own fantastic line of products.

The smell isn't great, but it feels like my skin had a big drink of water when I apply. It's so moisturizing. It is thicker than essences you may be used to. It quite literally is closer to the texture and feel of milk. It has helped my perioral dermatitis so much and this is now a permanent staple in my skincare routine. Be aware that if you are sensitive to coconut alkanes, this product may not be good for you. I have attached a photo of me holding the product and my skin after applying with not a stitch of makeup.

Author: itsfi
Title: Glowy hydration, just not the best fit for my skin
ReviewText:
I have the full size & mini versions of this product, both of which I purchased directly from the brand.

TL;DR: The product itself is very nice & I can see why it has a cult following. The skin on my face can only handle it in small doses. The skin on my body, however, soaks this up & appreciates how hydrating it is. Just as this can be used to thin down fuller coverage foundations, it can help to thin overly thick hand/foot/body creams, making it easier to spread.

WHAT I LIKE:
* Light, thin-ish, milky consistency
* Softly hydrating
* Hailey Bieber's tip to mix this with fuller coverage foundations to make a more skin-tint-like base is excellent

AREA(S) FOR IMPROVEMENT:
* Would love to be able to see how much product has been used/remains

FYI:
* Contains some fabulous skincare ingredients for dry/very dry skin in need of barrier repair
* Product itself is very nice. I can see why it has a cult following. On paper, my skin should love this, but, for some reason (that I suspect may be the coconut alkanes in it), my skin can become irritated if I'm using it too often, but once every so often in the cooler seasons, it's fine. 
* BEAUTY HACK: Usually, the skin on the body is less sensitive than the skin on the face & can tolerate products/ingredients that the skin on the face cannot. If that's true for you & this passes a patch test, you can (a) use it in lieu of body lotion/cream or (b) mix a little of this with a thick/too thick hand/foot/body cream to thin down the thicker cream, making it easier to spread. 
* Highly recommend getting a sample to try first, if you can, either in store or as a promo gwp.

BUY 🛍️ or BYE 👋🏼?:
* This really is a wonderfully hydrating formula; if you're not sensitive/allergic to coconut alkanes, it's worth looking into. BUY 🛍️
* I’ll use the beauty hack to use up what I have of the product but won’t repurchase BYE 👋🏼 

Sent from my iPhone

Title: Sticky but super hydrating
ReviewText:
The scent in the tube is a bit plasticky and sweet, but it’s barely noticeable once applied. It has a mild sugary taste, almost like you just took a sip of sweetened tea. The texture is quite fluid and definitely on the sticky side. A word of warning: if you have fine hair and like wearing it down, even the slightest breeze will have your hair glued to your lips.

I ordered this in the shade Espresso ☕️, and the color itself is stunning 😍 However, the applicator isn't the most user-friendly. Applying it straight from the tube is a bit tricky, and it takes some practice to get a neat, even finish. On my pale lips, a single layer is also a bit too sheer. While the color is buildable, applying a second layer to get that beautiful pigment makes it even stickier than before. For that reason, I’m knocking off one star.

As a makeup product, it’s not my favorite due to the tackiness, but as a treatment, it’s excellent. I apply it as the very first step of my makeup routine, and by the time I’m done with my brows and eyes, my lips look completely nourished and smooth.

Author: Rajwani
Title: Such a pretty tint it is.
ReviewText:
I’m big on lip tints, and I can never have enough of it. I need one in every bag so I’m never without it. The Rhode lip tint is perfectly sized for that. The cute, compact packaging makes it easy to carry and super handy.
The formula is hydrating and moisturizing, and since it’s enriched with shea butter, peptides, and vitamin E, it not only adds a tint but also nourishes the lips. I tried the shade Ribbon, a beautiful sheer pink that looks great on its own or layered over lipstick. I love the color, though my naturally pigmented lips make it blend softly with my natural tone.
I absolutely love the shine, hydration, and comfort it provides, and I can’t wait to try more shades. I’m all set to face the winter woes with these new lippies from Rhode.

Author: izzeye
Title: STINKY BLUE CHEESE SMELL - DONT BUY
ReviewText:
After having this lipgloss for a month it started to smell like blue cheese. I originally bought it the day they dropped Rhode in Sephora. At first everything was well but then it quickly turned south. Everytime I would apply on my lips I would get a sour waft of stinky blue cheese that would linger while wearing it.

What I’m most disappointed is the fact that when I went into store a few days past the 30 days from when I purchased, I was aware I couldn’t officially return, and the associate kept telling me how tons of people with this product were having the same issue. When I asked if it was from a bad batch she told me “no it’s just the product”. 

My question is if all of these $20 lip glosses are going to reek of pungent blue cheese after a few weeks of opening, then why are they still selling them?? Honestly ridiculous if you ask me. 

And if they did know this was going to be the case, this should have been forewarned prior to purchasing. With that being said I feel like I deserve some sort of refund for Sephora being deceiving about the peptides longevity. 

I am very disappointed and will not be repurchasing and STRONGLY do not recommend. (I do still love the pocket blushes)

Title: Save your money! It went bad in 30 days
ReviewText:
I don’t like doing this, but it was a terrible experience no one needs to go through. I have used the rhode Peptide Lip Treatment Nourishing Glaze previously and got excited they were going to sell it at Sephora.

 I purchased the lip tint on 9/8/25. I enjoyed it at first, the color is great and it lasted so I wasn’t constantly reapplying it. However, less than a month after purchasing, I noticed a VERY foul smelling odor. I thought maybe something got into the cap area so I cleaned it with alcohol. I tried again and realized it was the lip glaze producing the odor! I looked online and read that this is a common occurrence with this product, but all of the reviews I saw were after using the product for 6 months. I had it 29 days! I submitted a return online to drop off in store and explained the reason in the return. I received the return email with the barcode to provide to the in-store beauty advisor. 

 Today was the first day I was available to do the return, when the advisor scanned the barcode she said it was over 30 days so she couldn’t continue with the return. I was shocked, I said if she wasn’t going to accept the return then to just throw it away because that’s what I plan to do. She told me she couldn’t accept it at all. I am so disappointed, I am sticking to LANEIGE, because I’ve never had this type of issue with their product.

Author: itsfi
Title: Strikes the right balance for color and shine
ReviewText:
TL;DR: These hydrating lip tints strike the right balance for color (sheer but buildable) & shine - glassy & glossy without looking heavy, goopy or overly lacquered.

WHAT I LIKE:
* Glides on smoothly, easily - directly from the tube or with fingers
* Buildable tint - has a hint of sheer color but is buildable
* Feels comfortable on lips even when I've layered on 3 coats (for the lighter shades)
* Glassy, glossy finish - more than a soft sheen but not overly shiny - it doesn't give a lacquered, vinyl effect (it doesn't claim to)
* Good wear time even with sipping gently on liquids & light and careful snacking throughout the day - I can get 3, sometimes 4 hours, which is pretty good for a balm
* Contains peptides, which can promote cell turnover, reduce signs of aging around the lips, stimulate collagen production which can plump up lips

AREA(S) FOR IMPROVEMENT:
* Would love to see the color range expand. The formula lends nicely to deeper shades in that it makes vibrant, bold shades easily wearable with its initial sheer tint & buildability (especially for those of us who might be more timid when it comes to a bolder lip color)
* Design of the cap makes it challenging, if not impossible, to stand it upright without propping it against something. Not a dealbreaker.

FYI:
* Tint fades first, then the shine but the hydration from the lip treatment remains
* Color of the packaging meant to reflect the shade the particular tint can get to - I can build up to the color with about 2-3 coats - 3 for the lightest shades as my lips naturally have more pigment to them. Color on lips will have a less opacity just given the nature of it being a balm.
* The tints are typically unscented except for those that are / were part of a limited edition release
* Fits easily into the pocket of jeans, pants, dress, skirt, or purse
* Makes a great gift or stocking stuffer

BUY, BUY, BUY or BYE-BYE?:
* The formulation, level of shine & buildable color work for me. BUY

Author: hiptotheship
ReviewText: Gritty can mean it’s expired. Lip balm also becomes gritty from a process called "fat blooming" or crystallization, where fats with different melting points in natural butters, like cocoa butter or shea butter, melt and re-solidify at different rates due to temperature fluctuations. This slow cooling creates larger, grainy crystals within the balm, making it feel sandy. You can fix it by gently melting the balm and cooling it quickly, or by storing it at consistent room temperature.

Author: honeyi
ReviewText:
I’ve been using The Ordinary Niacinamide 10% + Zinc 1% Serum for a few months now, and it’s become a regular part of my skincare routine. I have combination skin with some oiliness in the T-zone and occasional breakouts. This serum really helps in keeping excess oil under control and visibly reduces the appearance of pores.

What I really like is that it’s lightweight, absorbs quickly, and doesn’t leave any sticky residue. It layers well under moisturizer and makeup, which is a big plus. After consistent use, I’ve noticed my skin looks more even-toned and feels smoother.

One thing to note is that it can cause some initial purging or slight irritation, especially if you’re new to actives or have sensitive skin. I recommend starting with a patch test and using it every other day at first.

Overall, this is a great affordable option if you’re looking to add niacinamide into your skincare routine. Just be patient and consistent with it!

Title: Beware - Caused Major Skin Reaction
ReviewText: I wish I could give this product 0 stars.  I do not have particularly sensitive skin, and I have been using 5% niacinamide from another brand for about a year with no issues.  I decided to try this because of all of the great reviews, but I should have paid more attention to the over 700 1 star reviews warning people about the damage that this product can do.  After a week of using 2 drops of this product mixed with my usual moisturizer every other day, I developed the worst rash of my life all over my face and neck, and my face was red, raw, and swollen.  My allergist had to put me on a 14 day course of prednisone to resolve it.  After looking at pictures and reading the stories of the 1 star reviews, I realized that what happened to me has happened to many other people who have used this product.  Please be mindful of the fact that even if you patch test (which I did) it could be a few days before your skin reacts badly to this product as this is what happened to me and seems to be a trend in some of the other reviews that I read.  This is truly the worst experience that I have ever had with a skincare product.  Please beware.

I’m 43, and I spent years doing little but wiping my face with a baby wipe at bedtime, and moisturizing maybe once a week.   

Fed up with how terrible my skin looked, in March I started using The Ordinary’s niacinamide in rotation with their mandelic acid + HA, washing at bedtime with their glycolic acid foaming cleanser, and using a Korean ceramide moisturizer nightly (Good Cera off Amazon), and Burt’s Bees calming moisturizer every morning. 

After one month of use I can hardly believe the difference in overall skin tone and texture. I won’t need to explain which is the Before and which is After in the two pics. They were taken at the same time of day in the same lighting conditions with the same phone, exactly 1 month and two days apart. A lot of the improvement is due to regular moisturizing, I know, but the niacinamide and mandelic acid absolutely evened out my skin tone enormously.

On top of that, what I thought was skin purging turned out to be a skin reaction, with thousands of what looked like whiteheads but were very watery.

After looking into it, it seems like someone like myself can’t handle the high formula of 10%. If you’re like me and you want to try a product like this START SLOW! Look for a product with a much lower percentage and don’t jump straight into the deep end like I did haha.

I hope this helps other skin product allergic people!

ReviewText:

After applying it to my face, I can easily put makeup on top without any peeling or pilling, which is very important to me. My foundation goes on smoothly and looks natural throughout the day. Another big plus is that it doesn’t sting my eyes, even when I apply it around the eye area. I usually have sensitive eyes with sunscreens, so this is a huge advantage for me.

I also like that I can reapply it in the middle of the day without my skin feeling overloaded. Because the texture is so lightweight, my face still feels fresh and comfortable after multiple applications. It doesn’t clog my pores or make my skin feel suffocated.

Overall, this sunscreen is perfect for daily use. It works well under makeup, feels gentle on the skin, and provides strong sun protection without irritation. I would definitely recommend this to anyone who loves Korean skincare or is looking for a lightweight, non-irritating sunscreen for everyday wear. I will definitely repurchase this product.

This has a dewy finish as the name implies, so another reason I can't use this on my face as it is very oily as it is, but has a lovely finish on my hands. I also notice the smell is different. Overall, very happy with this product.

Title: I Cannot Recommend This Product Enough!!!
ReviewText: [I received this product in exchange for my honest review] I can not even begin to describe how excited I was when I was chosen to review this product! Let’s start with the brand and why I think you should try out Beauty of Joseon. For starters, this brand focusing on creating skincare and beauty products that are gentle on the skin, enriching, and most importantly, effective. The cruelty free brand develops all of their products without animal testing which is always important to me. The products they sell are all inspired by traditional Hanbang- the Korean medicine based on natural ingredients with therapeutic benefits. If that isn’t enough to convince you that this brand is seriously amazing- let’s take a look at their individual products. The Day Dew Sunscreen I have recently been using is unreal! To begin, the packaging arrived with measures in place to ensure proper sanitation, which is always important to me when it comes to skin care. The box had a tape securement and a tinfoil cover on the tip of the bottle itself. Next, the 50mL bottle is the perfect size to bring with you anywhere, it fits in any bag and comes with me wherever I leave the house so I can reapply on the go. The sunscreen itself has a light scent that is quite refreshing, not overbearing at all like other sunscreens I have tried. Additionally, the sunscreen leaves absolutely zero white cast, so it works perfectly in my day to day life, whether I’m wearing makeup or not. When using this product, I feel clean and not like I am being weighed down by an oily face. It is SPF 50 which is wonderful for preventing any sun damage or future wrinkles. The ingredients are clean and clearly stated on the box and bottle. All in all, I cannot recommend this product enough. The brand and the product speak for themselves- it is the best of the best! Thank you Beauty of Joseon!

Author: MsReporter
Title: An interesting take on the US sunscreen
ReviewText:
Don't let the 4-star rating intimidate you. Here is my honest take about this product:
- The texture is milky, blends in seamlessly and most importantly, does NOT leave a white cast. Huge W. Thus, if you like milky sunscreen, this is for you.
- However, one thing I don't like about this product which also explains the lack of one star is that this product used the outdated filters from the FDA, so when you apply the sunscreen, there will be this funky smell from the filters used, although they do fade away quickly compared to mainstream US sunscreens.

Conclusion:
Would I say that this is BoJ's best take on American sunscreen? Yes.
Would I say that this is comparable to Relief Sun and Aqua Fresh aka the originals? lol no
But yeah, it is indeed a decent sunscreen and performs better than your average sunscreen, even under FDA's silly restrictions. It is worth a try - but would I repurchase it? Meh.

Title: Not the same as Relief Sun Rice + Probiotic SPF 50
ReviewText: I was a huge fan of the Beauty of Joseon Relief Sun Rice + Probiotic SPF 50 sunscreen. Unfortunately, due to the FDA's glacial processes for approval of sunscreens, the sale of that original formula was discontinued in the USA in January 2025 and BoJ came up with a "US only" formula that adheres to the older US approved UV filters. You can no longer purchase the original formula (at least from the official site) which has more up to date and more effective sun protection (including UVA rays) along with a much lighter, comfortable formula. It's a real shame that we don't have access to these more advanced sunscreens in the US. This Day Dew Sunscreen is still nice, although it has that distinct "sunscreen" smell that conventional sunscreens have and also has that mineral-oil quality I dislike about them. It's still better than most though and I would use it on my body: for daily facial sunscreen though I'm afraid the US is still in the dark ages.

I was shocked to find my skin loves this sunscreen more than any other I’ve ever tried, mineral or chemical. Yes, I would prefer the newer SPF filters used in Europe and South Korea, but with very rare exception those sunscreens include high levels of propanediol, alcohol, and other ingredients my skin doesn’t tolerate. This new BOJ sunscreen dries down to a dewy but not greasy finish and works beautifully under makeup. I absolutely love it and hope it’s a big success for BOJ. The price is also quite reasonable. Highly recommend giving it a try.

Title: Worth Every Bit of the Hype
ReviewText:
First, let me start by saying this is absolutely worth the hype. I’m a lip girl through and through — I love a great lip balm, gloss, anything — and this one delivers.

It makes my lips feel lush, luscious, and deeply hydrated. The texture is smooth, cushiony, and comfortable without feeling sticky. It gives the perfect glossy, healthy shine while actually moisturizing at the same time.

What really impressed me is that the hydration lasts. My lips still feel soft even after the shine fades a bit, which tells me it’s actually nourishing and not just sitting on top of the lips. The gloss factor is beautiful — juicy but not over-the-top — and it wears comfortably for hours.

10/10 — this is a must-buy. I literally just ordered the new shade that dropped and can’t wait to review that one too.

If you’re on the fence about purchasing, go ahead and jump over it and grab one. You will not be disappointed.

Author: meeggymoo
Title: HOLY GRAIL!!!
ReviewText: I genuinely think anyone leaving less than a 5-star review may not fully understand how this product is meant to be used. This is a treatment; it’s designed to heal your lips, not act as a regular, constantly reapplied lip balm. You only need to use it a few times a day at most. I typically apply it in the morning and mid-day, and sometimes at night if my lips are especially dry (like in the winter). I reach for it when my lips are close to peeling or feel super dehydrated. This is not something you should be reapplying every hour. Your lips may start peeling; that’s because it exfoliates. It’s doing its job. You use it when you’re dry, let it work, and that’s it. One application literally heals my husband’s lips (and mine). In between treatments, you’ll want a traditional moisturizing balm to keep your lips comfortable and hydrated. This is where other brands come in. Jack Black (their SPF balm), Cocokind, and Summer Fridays are great for maintaining moisture throughout the day. They won’t heal your lips the way EADEM does, but they’re perfect between treatments. Ole Henriksen is another option that both heals and can be reapplied more frequently, but for me it feels more like a lip gloss; a bit stickier. I don’t usually reach for it on no-makeup days, but I always use it when I’m wearing makeup. For me, EADEM is truly superior. Ole Henriksen is my second favorite, and I love Cocokind and Jack Black for in-between hydration.

Author: themamacheetah
Title: Not all colors are as fabulous
ReviewText:
So…docking a star because of inconsistency, color selection, and representation. I first bought bissap glaze. Color appeared to be a great choice for me, but once ON, it looked muddy and vampy. I had also tried the butter mochi in-store and it lasted through the rest of my shopping trip. But the bissap seemed to parch my lips a bit and didn’t last long. I decided to return that try again anyway, having had a better experience from my previous shopping trip. I grabbed both limited edition shades once restocked and then came back and grabbed a second croissant to keep in my bathroom drawer. Both these colors are really nice. Applying the chocolate too thick does look like you have melted chocolate on your lips but that blots out to a nice sheer shimmer, and it legit smells like I just put a chocolate in my mouth. However, there is ZERO taste, which I greatly appreciate. The croissant one is more subtle so I only noticed a scent the first couple of times I used it, but again no taste. 

It stays glossy a really decent amount of time, and then dries down to more of a seal on your lips rather than wearing off. So it’s been really nice for sealing moisture IN plus works beautifully on top of my lip stain to seal and preserve the color longer. (Also a better option for kissing since it’s sort of a film former that doesn’t slip around.) It does seem to have a very mild exfoliating effect and I have smooth, soft lips that take my stain nicely and evenly. (And it’s winter as I write this!) I will still alternate this with my Alpyn lip balm and a more traditional cocoa butter based stick because they perform in different ways and nourish differently, but this balm has become a purse staple now. Really great product if you find a color that works for you. I need more light/bright shades though because the only color (not just shimmer) that really works for my coloring is the guava, but I cannot tolerate the smell. It hits like BO to me.

Author: versacevonna
Title: Disappointing 'scent'/shade, terrific product.
ReviewText:
I'm super confused. I've never purchased this product, or from this brand before. I bought shade "Croissant au Beurre". 
When I tell you it has no smell, whatsoever, I don't mean 'oh, it could be stronger' or 'it's too bad the scent is so light and doesn't punch you in the face like Summer Fridays or Rhode', I mean it doesn't have ANY scent. If you were even sensitive to scents(I'm not), this would be fragrance-free to you. Not being dramatic.
All the reviews about the product itself are accurate. Even though there's glitter in it, you can't feel even the slightest grittiness; it's completely smooth and very hydrating and long lasting. I thought even the "metal tip" was going to be gimmicky, because why would how it applies really matter? But it actually is super nice and noticeably different from all the other lippies I own, it's just completely fragrance free though. 
That's disappointing to me because even though the product itself is one of the best lip products I've now used, I was expecting some delicious(I didn't even care if it would've been super light) fragrance. It's just an expensive, clear(only you can see the glitter), fragrance free gloss with a nice applicator. 
I genuinely bought the product for the scent. I mean, seriously, how many lippies do you have that smell like a "buttery pastry"? That would've been cool!
For me, I still have none. 
Don't let this review deter you from purchasing this lip product, but definitely don't expect much if you're buying shade "Croissant au Beurre".

Author: SunniDeeMe
Title: Proceed with Caution
ReviewText: I originally loved this product so much that I bought 3 shades. Very moisturizing (not just sitting on top of the lips) and I did not need to re-apply even after eating, drinking, "gyming", etc. Everything was fine and dandy until I wore this stuff in the summer time...my lips got sunburned! Sadly, I have been struggling for the past 2 months to get my lips back to normal from a pretty severe reaction. Initially, my top lip was swollen and puffy and the corners of my mouth kept splitting. Then the hyperpigmentation and peeling came. I never knew that lips could get sunburned until I used this product! If I am not mistaken, it has 3 exfoliating ingredients in it, including LACTIC ACID. For the life of me, I truly don't understand why any amount of lactic acid would be in a product with any sort of warning/suggestion to avoid sun exposure, wear sunscreen, etc. This is extremely negligent on the company's behalf, despite how much I initially loved the product. I plan to try it again in the colder months once my lips have healed and sunny weather is long gone. I however would be very leery of purchasing this product. Just be aware and careful should you choose to still try it.

Author: samisaywhat
Title: Works on my Accutane Lips
ReviewText: I’ve been on Accutane twice now and anyone that’s been on it knows how badly it dries out your lips. After my first time it took a couple of months for my lips to bounce back. Second time? Girl. My lips are still dry! It’s been months! I’ve tried maybe a hundred products to keep my lips hydrated. I’ve tried lip basting. Vaseline. And Vaseline was the only product that kind of worked but I’m not trying to stick my finger in a jar while I’m on the run, and their lip formula isn’t just pure Vaseline either. So I tried Eadem. I didn’t want to like it. $24!? But I’m desperate so I purchased it. I got Boba Bounce first and was… shocked. I didn’t have to reapply 20 times a day. My lips didn’t peel from the color. I got Butter Mochi after that (it’s never in stock so was a huge win) and the it’s even better. Colored balms always leave some kind of residue so you have to fully wipe it off before your 3rd or 4th application. But Butter Mochi leaves no residue. It hydrates and locks in that hydration. It truly does smooth my lips out. I will say the texture is pretty thick but as someone that wore nothing but Vaseline it’s not a negative at all. And I love the metal applicator. So unfortunately (for my wallet) I will be repurchasing.

Title: Beautiful Product
ReviewText: I’m normally not one to spend over $20 on a lip balm, but I was drawn in after hearing how nourishing they are for the lips, while also giving pigment, in colors that show up on brown skin. My first shade was Boba Bounce because I don’t have a brown gloss, and I was so impressed. It smells like brown sugar boba, yet the fragrance doesn’t irritate my lips, and it looks good. I think it would flatter many skin tones. As a gloss, it’s not transfer-proof, but I don’t really expect that. It does go on a bit patchy because it’s so pigmented, so it may not be for you, if you prefer to reapply without a mirror. Massaging it in with the applicator works just fine. This does the work of both a lip balm and a gloss, and it’s a treatment too. I no longer have to worry about dry or flaky lips with this. I also have Bissap Glaze, which is like a berry on my lips, and Guava, which is a bright berry pink. They show up and I’m light-medium to medium skin tone.

ReviewText: I actually want to give this 5 full stars for the product itself. I deal with incredibly dry and flaky lips and skin due to medical conditions and medications. Title: My new summer go to!
ReviewText:
I love lip balms (my favorites of all time are are the clear Summer Fridays and Ole Henriksen balms and I don't like the Rhode lipbalm since it was too thin for me for a reference) and bought this myself. This one has skyrocketed to one of my most used. The scent is like a real guava and it's so nice! I can really see it being not sweet enough for people, but I love natural fruit scents like this that don't go into candy or perfume territory. I think the other Eadem scents might be too strong for me personally and I recommend smelling them in store first (I have the same problem with the Ole Henriksen balms outside of the citrus and strawberry ones but I like most of the Summer Fridays scents).

The color is a really beautiful medium pink on my light-medium olive skin tone and is already going to be my pink summer lip of choice. The balm itself is thicker with a really pretty gloss that reminds me the most of the Ole Henriksen balms (the Summer Fridays are a little more liquidy and spread more), but with a lot more pigment. It lasts a long time on my lips, I've worn it before bed and woken up feeling it on my lips still. I also really like the metal applicator, even though I do find the tube hard to squeeze sometimes.

Title: The best lip balm I’ve ever! A new purse staple.

I recently tried the EADEM Le Chouchou Lip Softening Balm, and I can confidently say it’s earned a permanent spot in my bag. From the first application, I was hooked the formula is incredibly hydrating, yet lightweight enough to feel comfortable throughout the day.  

One of the standout features is how long it lasts. Unlike other balms that need constant reapplication, this one keeps my lips soft and nourished for hours. The texture is rich but not overly thick, providing the perfect balance of moisture and a natural gloss without feeling sticky.  

I also love the cooling metal applicator, which makes each application feel soothing and luxurious. The subtle tint in Boba Bounce adds just the right amount of color, enhancing my natural lip tone effortlessly.  

Overall, this balm is a game-changer for anyone looking for long-lasting hydration, a touch of shine, and a truly enjoyable experience. EADEM has delivered a formula that feels amazing, works beautifully, and is now a staple in my daily routine.

Author: bswitz
Title: Game changer
ReviewText:
I’m 35F, live in the Midwest, and sometimes have low vitamin D. I’m constantly looking for a lip product to hydrate my lips - bonus if it has pigment. 

Usually lip products are grainy, dry my lips out, or wear off fast (or all 3.) 

I purchased this and have been using it for a month. The applicator feels very smooth and the silver look to the tube is visually appealing, so much so my toddler steals it constantly when he sees it out. 

The formula is unlike any I’ve ever used — it’s hydrating, smooth, smells good, has great pigment AND MOST OF ALL, I can apply it before I go to sleep, and when I wake up in the morning, I still feel it on my lips! I have tried nearly every lip product on the market, and this is the first to do that for me — lasted throughout the night (I’m undoubtedly a bit of an open mouth sleeper,) and my lips were hydrated come morning. 

If you’re on the fence about buying, do it. You can feel the difference, literally. 

Eadem is setting the bar for lip products out there — I’ll be a faithful customer for life.

Title: Eadem Chouchou Lip Balm – Honest Review
ReviewText:
I really wanted to love this lip balm. The metal tip applicator feels luxe and cooling on the lips, and the formula itself is beautifully cushiony and hydrating—everything I usually look for in a balm. I went with the clear shade because the colored versions, while gorgeous, seemed a bit more pigmented than I typically prefer.

That said, I have to return it. The biggest issue for me is the taste. Since it’s unflavored, you really taste the raw formula, and unfortunately, I find it extremely unpleasant. It’s not a subtle aftertaste—it lingers, and I just couldn't get used to it, even after a full day of wear. It completely ruined the experience of an otherwise great formula.

It’s such a shame because the texture is spot-on, and I had high hopes. Maybe the flavored or tinted versions mask the taste better when sheered out, but for now, this one just isn’t for me.

Author: Estellajmv
Title: Good But Could Be Great
ReviewText:
It really is an excellent lip balm. It reminds me of the old Fitglow lip balms that were the gold standard for longevity, moisture and how they feel on the lips. However - a few things need to be tweaked before the hype is warranted here. 

First, either produce enough product or don't put it on the market. The false scarcity sales tactic is so tired, and this shade "sold out" minutes into its release. Other shades keep going in and out of stock as well. Second, my local Sephora randomly had a tester for this shade a day after its release online, and it is NOT the "hazy pink" shade its described to be. It's more of a sheer warm red. The shade in person looks more like the swatch online for fig sauce, although fig sauce AND guava fresca are both much warmer in person. Again - not sure why brands do this thing of making every swatch look cooler in photos than the product is in person. Lastly - and this is just nitpicking, but the product can be a challenge to squeeze out if it's not warm. 

I'd highly recommend swatching in person before you buy, or just go with the clear version...IF you can find it in stock. I hope they produce more colors with accurate swatches in more realistic quantities. Then it could be just about perfect.

Author: skinwithdee
ReviewText:
if you’re looking for a tinted lip balm that actually makes your lips softer and plumper the more you wear it, the eadem le chou chou lip softening balm is such a great option. it has a thick texture that feels very plush and cushiony on the lips, and it delivers pretty long-lasting moisture. the shade i have is boba bounce, which is a medium-deep brown. the metal packaging and applicator feel super luxurious and cooling when i apply it on my lips.

i don’t particularly love the scent of the lip balm–it’s a bit overly sweet for me. also, because of the level of pigment in the product and the heavy applicator, it can take a long time to get an even layer of color on your lips. and i find that the flat applicator gets messy easily too. despite these shortcomings, i think the formula, shade, and finish make it worth it!

Title: There are way better similar products out there
ReviewText:
The formula is so thick that even during this hot summer I struggle to squeeze any product out of the tube. It also sits on my lips without ever being absorbed. I don't feel any softening or exfoliating, just a glob of product that sits there, on top of my lips. 

Even though the product is supposed to be clear, it leaves a white film or cast on my lips, dulling their natural color and making them look weird. Not even in a stylistic way.

The cooling metal applicator is nice, but I usually associate such applicators with under eye products; here it feels a bit gimmicky. 

To top it all off, literally, the way the cap is designed gets product stuck in it with no way to clean it or get it out. 

It's way too expensive to not deliver on its claims. You might honestly do better with a tub of vaseline. But I recommend looking at other similar offerings.

Author: letrainfalldown
Title: Interesting concept but not my favorite.
ReviewText:
I got the shade Burnt Malai because I wanted something fairly neutral. I like the shade - it's a bit darker than expected but I guess it's a good shade to have in my repertoire!
The applicator is a cool idea, but is better in theory than practice - it's metal with a sloping tip, but it ended up making a bit of a mess when I used it. I think you'll have to clean it off (or use way less product) every time in order to not make a mess inside the cap 😅
The product smells really good! Almost like sugar cookie batter or something. 
Even though it's called a balm, it's more of a thick lip gloss than a balm. It's like a paste and ends up making my lips fairly shiny, which I would've have expected (and honestly would prefer not to) from a balm. But my lips were a bit dry and it does its job and my lips look pretty hydrated now. I did notice a bit of a funny sensation on my lips - it's kind of cooling or something? 
Overall, interesting product although not my favorite - the applicator especially needs work (although the squeeze tube is an interesting idea too.)

Title: More then just a lip balm !
ReviewText:
💋 Hey beauties! Today, I’m beyond excited to share my thoughts on a new holy grail product that has completely transformed my lip care routine – the EADEM Lip Softening Balm in the shade Milky Desert Rose. 

💋From the moment I first applied this balm, I noticed an immediate difference. The formula is incredibly smooth and glides on like a dream, thanks to EADEM’s innovative SpreadIt™ Polymer Technology. It’s not just a balm – it’s an experience. The texture is ultra-comfy and non-sticky, which is a huge plus for me. I love that it provides a glossy finish without that annoying tacky feeling.

💋Now, let’s talk about the magic ingredients. This balm is packed with Hibiscus Enzymes and Lactic Acid, which work together to gently exfoliate and buff away dry, flaky skin. This means my lips can better absorb all the rich moisture that the balm has to offer.

💋The Brazilian Açaí and African Mongongo Butters are absolute superstars in this formula. They intensely nourish and lock in moisture, ensuring my lips stay hydrated and protected throughout the day. Plus, these butters are loaded with protective antioxidants, which is always a bonus.

💋But the true standout for me is the Collagen-Boosting Peptide. Not only does it restore a supple feel to my lips, but it also visibly reduces fine lines, giving my lips a naturally plump and youthful look. Say goodbye to lip wrinkles!

The Milky Desert Rose shade is the perfect everyday color – it adds a subtle flush of color that’s just enough to make your lips look healthy and vibrant without being overpowering. It’s ideal for all skin types and is especially great if you’re dealing with concerns like dryness, dullness, or fine lines and wrinkles.

💋Another thing I love about this balm is that it’s gluten-free and cruelty-free, so I can feel good about what I’m putting on my lips.

💋 The EADEM Lip Softening Balm in Milky Desert Rose is a must-have for anyone looking to achieve smoother, softer, and more hydrated lips.

ReviewText:

The formula is lightweight and absorbs quickly, but it can feel a little tingly—especially if your skin barrier is sensitive or if you’ve exfoliated recently. On those days, I either skip it or layer a hydrating toner first, which works perfectly.

I think the key is not to use it every single day right away. Once you build up tolerance, it’s honestly amazing. My skin looks more even and more “awake” since I added it to my routine.

Overall: Effective, not too strong, and actually delivers results. Just listen to your skin and adjust the frequency if needed.

Author: Justinemarienav
Title: Holy Grail Multi-Tasker!
ReviewText:
This is my unbiased review! No incentives or anything, purchased on my own and I'm OBSESSED!

I've been using The Ordinary's 7% Glycolic Acid Exfoliating and Brightening Daily Toner for a while now, and it's truly become a staple in my routine.

For my face, I incorporate this powerful toner into my P.M. routine just twice a week. Consistency is key, especially with active ingredients, so I always follow it up with a hydrating powerhouse. My routine looks like this: after cleansing, I apply the Glycolic Acid Toner, then layer with The Inkey List's Hyaluronic Acid Serum (my absolute favorite for a hydration boost), and lock it all in with an intensely rich moisturizer like La Roche-Posay Cicaplast Balm B5. The results? My skin has never been clearer, completely free of breakouts. It feels incredibly smooth to the touch, and I've noticed a significant improvement in my overall complexion – it's much more even and radiant.

But here's where this toner truly shines as a multi-tasker for me: its incredible effectiveness on my body. After I shower and shave my bikini line, I immediately apply this Glycolic Acid Toner to the area(bikini line ONLY****) I then follow up with either my Naturium Bio-Lipid Restoring Body Lotion or Neutrogena Hydro Boost Body Gel Cream (depending on what I have on hand!), and the difference is phenomenal. It has completely eliminated any razor bumps, irritation, and, most importantly, those pesky ingrown hairs that used to be a constant struggle.

This isn't just a toner; it's a versatile solution for both face and body. If you're looking for a product that delivers on its promises – from clearer, smoother facial skin to banishing post-shave issues – The Ordinary's 7% Glycolic Acid Toner is an absolute must-try. Highly recommend!

Title: Holy Grail for Skin Texture & Hyperpigmentation
ReviewText:
I can’t recommend this glycolic acid toner from The Ordinary enough! It’s absolutely amazing for anyone struggling with rough, bumpy skin texture. I use it every night, gently patting it on my face with a cotton pad, and by the next morning, my skin feels incredibly smooth and soft. No more dullness—my skin looks brighter and refreshed!

It’s also helped with my hyperpigmentation. Over time, I’ve noticed a reduction in the dark spots, and it’s made my complexion look more even. It does wonders for exfoliating and removing dead skin cells, leaving my skin feeling rejuvenated.

I always follow up with a moisturizer to keep my skin hydrated, and it’s become a holy grail product I couldn’t live without. If you have skin texture issues or pigmentation concerns, this is definitely worth trying!

Highly recommend!

If you’re struggling with dark underarms or persistent odor, I highly recommend giving The Ordinary Glycolic Acid 7% Toning Solution a try. It has made such a positive difference for me!

Author: itsfi
Title: I get the hype now
ReviewText:
SKIN TYPE & CONCERNS: 
* Normal -to-dry / combo in summer
* Year-round - mild rosacea on cheeks, redness around nose, occasional clogged pores along jawline; slightly compromised skin barrier; dehydrated, sensitive skin 
* Summer - breakouts periodically on chin; enlarged pores on nose; excess sebum on lower T-zone

USAGE: 
* 5-6 days per week for almost 4+ weeks in a mild climate as part of evening skincare routine 
* Multiple times per day for almost a week in warm & humid setting & to hydrate skin in-flight to/from 

TL;DR: I never understood the hype with this product … until now. I purchased this when it first came out in 2019 & have received it as gratis on a few occasions since then, including a month ago. With first use, it just didn’t do anything, good or bad, to my skin. My skin has changed since I first tried this. To my surprise, it’s turned out to do a nice job keeping my skin clean, reducing redness, & helping to heal & soothe cuts & scrapes. 👍🏼

WHAT I LIKE: 
* Helps calm & soothe redness, in both milder & humid climates
* Good for sensitive skin 
* Lightly hydrating 
* Disinfecting / antibacterial properties with cuts & scrapes - I experienced some minor cuts & scrapes on my hands & legs while on vacay & spritzed this spray on those areas to keep them clean & speed up the healing process 
* Helped with managing / caring for a zit that surfaced while on vacay

AREA(S) FOR IMPROVEMENT: 
* Minor issue - wish it didn’t have the swimming pool scent

FYI:  
* I picked up a scent from this spray a few times (not every time), reminiscent of a swimming pool. It wasn’t too pronounced & did not linger but it was noticeable. 
* Seems like it’s better or best suited for those with oily, normal or combo skin. May not be great for those with very dry skin. 

BUY, BUY, BUY 🛍️ or BYE-BYE 👋🏼?:
* This is something I would use in the warmer months or if I’m traveling someplace with high humidity. BUY 🛍️

Title: Met My Expectations
ReviewText: First of all I want to say the size is perfect for on the go and minimal sized make-up bags. This was my first hypochlorous acid spray and it did exactly as described for me. Since then I’ve found lower priced versions from other companies with more product and I prefer to use those now. Hypochlorous acid is antimicrobial, antibacterial, and reduces inflammation so that’s what I used it for. Times when my skin felt irritated, itchy, and/or hot. Times when my face was super oily to the point where my eyes would burn after a long day. I’ve used it as a cleaner when I didn’t have hand sanitizer with me. I’ve used it if I had a cut. In all those instances it helped. What I’ve learned from dermatologists who make videos on YouTube is that this is great for irritation due to sweating (sometimes I’ve sprayed it on an irritated area, left it on for a little and wiped it off after). I also learned that if used too soon before or after other skincare products it can cause irritation. So to whoever decides to buy this, think of it as more of a gentle cleaner/refresher for your skin, face and body.

Title: Skin clearer, resolved eye eczema
ReviewText: I have significant redness and regularly get eczema around my eyes. I also get significant break outs along me cheek and jawline when traveling. Spraying my face before and after masking made a big difference - usually after flying I have multiple deep, cystic zits. This time I had a small surface one. When I let the spray dry then apply a barrier repair cream near my eye, I found the combo cleared up my light eye eczema within a week. There is a light chlorine smell but it fades. I did not have a reaction but if you're extra sensitive consider a wrist patch test for a day before trying. I tried the travel size first, then bought the value size to keep refilling it. When I'm traveling or sweaty I use it multiple times per day. When I'm just maintaining my skin I only use it every other day to reduce the risk of over drying. -- This wasn't an issue but one day I noticed my skin felt drier so I added this. Also make sure if you're using topical and hopefully sunscreen you read up on how to use them with this. Order matters from what I've seen derms post. Apologies for no before/after photos but my partner complimented my skin this week and I realized this was the difference.

Author: Amilaonaire
Title: Magic in a bottle
ReviewText:
I've attached photos but I have/had this really stubborn acne on my jaw/neck area for a while now that just WOULD NOT BUDGE. I used salicylic acid, glycolic acid, ALL of my tried and trues -- thing's I've done in the past and just KNOW work and nothing was working! I even use tretinoin on my face for acne, but when I'd put it on this region it made it super sensitive so I had to step back from that. 

I finally gave this spray a try and I'm genuinely blown away. In 24 hours my skin calmed down so much. The redness dissipated and I could finally see what exactly I was dealing with. It was really hard tiny pimples. I kept using this spray for a few more days and the actual acne is gone 99% at least and I'm only left with some hyperpigmentation which will go away with time and I will continue to use gentle exfoliating treatments for that (I'm not tripping about it). 

I just cannot express how grateful I am for hypochlorous acid lol THAT BEING SAID, yes you can definitely get this cheaper at the drugstore. I'm actually considering using what is left of this and getting a refill elsewhere.

Additionally, yes T28 may be overpricing this but I am grateful that they kind of put hypochlorous acid spray in the beauty market frfr. Like yes it existed but how many of us REALLY knew to reach for it for acne or redness? I know for a fact I didn't know and watching/reading things about it, it seems many didn't know either. 

I think the bottle for this spray is really nice. It mists very well and evenly. I'm keeping the bottle LOL 

It's also so gentle and not drying at all. I also DO use it with my other treatments. I use it with tretinoin. No issues.. I think you just have to let it dry before moving forward with your routine so requires some patience. 

Also, smells like pool water lol interesting scent but not "bad" by any means. 

For me: very effective, gentle acne and redness treatment. 10/10 would recommend and WILL repurchase.

Title: Damaged my barrier
ReviewText: Not to be dramatic, but this stuff is the devil. I purchased the travel size to treat a couple jaw pimples. Nothing major, mostly annoying and I thought I would try something low-rsk and new out. I have a paired down routine where I use tret at night a couple times a week, and Dieux Instant and Air Angel as well as Korean sunscreen (Purito). I used the spray twice; once after a shower and then before bed before my nightly routine. Yes, I let it dry down and didn't go crazy with it. My bottom lip swelled out with a pimple on my lip line, and I developed medium cysts on my lower face and jawline where the spray was concentrated. I then developed texture, redness and burning irritation that accompanies a damaged skin barrier over the next two days, although of course I didn't use the spray again. Moral of the story, as you can imagine, is PATCH TEST before using. Everything I read online indicated this would be safe for my skin. Jokes on me!

Author: Kbeth88
Title: Get your glass skin on!
ReviewText:
I’ve tried my fair share of sheet masks over the years, but the Biodance Bio-Collagen Real Deep Mask honestly stands out in a way that surprised me. I initially picked it up because of all the buzz around its “bio-collagen” technology and how it claims to deliver a spa-like treatment at home. After a few uses, I can confidently say it lives up to the hype — and then some. First, let’s talk fit and feel. This mask adheres to the face like a second skin — no slipping or air bubbles — which is rare. It’s made with this unique jelly-like material that feels ultra-soothing and cool the second you apply it. Unlike typical sheet masks that start drying out halfway through, this one stays moist and delivers a continuous surge of hydration. Now for the results: instant glow. Every time I’ve used it, my skin looks visibly plumper and smoother right after. Fine lines seem softer, and there’s this firm, bouncy feeling to my face that wasn’t there before. It’s like my skin got a tall glass of water and a collagen boost all at once. 
The only thing I’ll say is that it’s more of a treat than an everyday product, especially price-wise. But if your skin is feeling dull, dry, or tired — or if you just want to pamper yourself — this is 100% worth it. I now keep a few on hand for when my skin needs a serious boost.

Author: NoodleZ120
Title: Great hydration mask
ReviewText:
I had the chance to try the Biodance Bio-Collagen Real Deep Mask, and it was definitely an experience. The instructions say to leave it on your face for at least 3 to 4 hours, or even overnight. I didn’t want to risk messing it up or missing out on the full benefits while sleeping, so thankfully, since I work from home, I had no issue trying it out during the day.

I did my usual skin prep beforehand. At first glance, it seems like a typical sheet mask — all slimy and gooey — but the texture of this one reminded me of a super thin slice of Jell-O. It’s not as fragile as Jell-O, but I did accidentally tear it slightly with a nail. Fortunately, it didn’t affect the mask’s performance.

I liked that it comes in two parts, making it easier to fit different face shapes. There were leftover pieces for the eyes and mouth, which I placed under my boyfriend’s eyes and on the center of his forehead — surprisingly, it worked for all face sizes! I definitely felt like Dwight from The Office during the CPR training scene… IFYKYK.

Around the 2-hour mark, I noticed the mask slowly started changing color. By the 3-hour mark, about 95% of the essence had absorbed. Once fully absorbed, the mask felt like stretched-out plastic. The areas with overlap — and around one of my eyes — didn’t absorb quite as well, so I repositioned those sections for a bit longer.

After removing it, my skin felt super hydrated and glowing. I actually enjoyed the whole experience. I’d recommend saving this mask for a self-care day or an at-home spa session while binge-watching your favorite shows. I’d definitely repurchase and try their other masks.

Title: Good but not great
ReviewText:
This mask provides deep hydration and leaves your skin feeling soft and supple while delivering an even, glowy complexion. However, the product is difficult to apply, falls apart during use, and doesn’t fully deliver on pore minimization.

What I loved:
	•	The product offers some comfort and relaxation during use.
	•	The hydration effects were noticeable even after one use.
	•	My face felt plumper, glowy, and soft afterward.

What could be improved:
	•	Applying the product is cumbersome, and my mask ripped in multiple places during application.
	•	The mask doesn’t sit well on the face, even during minimal movement. It peeled at the edges and never felt secure.
	•	While the instructions suggest overnight wear is possible, I’m highly skeptical it would stay on for more than twenty minutes or through normal sleep movements.
	•	The effects didn’t fully live up to the hype, especially regarding pore minimization.
	•	The mask barely lasts three hours before falling apart, although the instructions recommend 3–4 hours for full benefits.

Ultimately, the mask does deliver deep hydration and can be a nice way to feel pampered if you’re lounging for a few hours, but it earns 3.5 stars at most. The delicacy and effort required to apply and maintain the mask on your face aren’t justified by the results.

However, I would still recommend it to anyone looking for a megadose of hydration during a lengthy movie or TV marathon, provided you’re prepared to handle it carefully and manage your expectations.

Author: tammeyg
Title: Easily applied & Felt great.
ReviewText:
This product was provided for promotional purposes in exchange for my honest review.

Upon opening the package, I was pleasantly surprised to find there was absolutely no smell or scent to the product. It was well-packaged, and the mask peeled easily from a thick plastic liner. The design features two separate pieces—one for the upper face and one for the lower—making application more convenient and customizable.

The mask itself is thick, gel-like, and saturated (but not dripping wet), which made it easy to apply. While adjusting the mask around my eyes, it did tear slightly in a couple of areas, but overall it remained intact and comfortable. It’s recommended to wear for at least three hours or even overnight. Personally, I found it unrealistic to wear it while sleeping, as it would likely fall off, but I did make it to the three-hour mark.

After use, the mask dried to a nearly transparent film and peeled off easily with no residue left behind. I didn’t feel the need to rinse my face afterward. My skin felt noticeably hydrated and refreshed. As for fine lines or wrinkle reduction, I didn’t observe much change after just one use—but that’s to be expected. I believe consistent, weekly use would provide more visible results over time.

All in all, I would recommend the BioDance Real Deep Collagen Face Mask for anyone looking to boost hydration and treat themselves to a self-care skincare moment. I’d likely purchase it myself to incorporate into my skin routine.

Author: ahahahhahahah
ReviewText: I had high hopes for the Biodance Bio-Collagen Real Deep Mask, especially after seeing so many positive reviews about its deep hydration and firming effects. After using it a few times, I have mixed feelings. Pros: ✅ Super hydrating – My skin definitely felt plumper and more moisturized after using it. It’s a great option for long flights or when my skin feels extra dry. ✅ Good fit – The hydrogel texture sticks well to my face and doesn’t slide around like some sheet masks do. ✅ Packed with skincare benefits – It contains niacinamide (great for brightening) and collagen (for skin elasticity), which are always a plus in my book. Cons: ❌ Feels a bit suffocating – Since it’s a hydrogel mask, it has a slightly occlusive feel, and after an hour or so, my skin started feeling a bit oily instead of refreshed. ❌ Fragile material – The mask is very soft and jelly-like, but also quite delicate. I accidentally tore a piece when adjusting it with my nails. ❌ Long wear time – It’s designed to be worn for 3–4 hours, which is way longer than most masks. While this might be great for people who like extended skincare routines, I don’t always have that much time to spare. Would I repurchase? Maybe for travel. I can see this being useful for long-haul flights when I want something hydrating that lasts. However, for everyday use, I prefer a mask that feels lighter and doesn’t require such a long wear time. If you love hydrogel masks and don’t mind a long treatment session, you might really enjoy this one. But if you prefer quick and breathable hydration, this might not be the best choice.

There’s a light, clean scent to it—barely noticeable, and it didn’t linger or bother me during the night. I really appreciated how breathable it felt too; even though it’s a hydrating mask, it didn’t suffocate my skin or feel heavy. This is a great overnight mask if you’re looking to boost hydration, improve skin texture, and get that “glass skin” effect by morning. It feels luxe, but without being too rich or greasy—perfect for dry to normal skin types. I’ll definitely be keeping this in rotation, especially on nights when my skin needs a little extra care.

Title: Hydrates & refreshes while providing a soft glow
ReviewText:
I purchased the mist directly from the brand and have been reaching for it at least a few days each week for the past 9 weeks.

TL:DR: A fine, light mist that hydrates & refreshes skin while providing a soft glow. 

WHAT I LIKE:
* Very fine, light mist
* Pump is easy to use - no jamming, clogging
* Feels hydrating, refreshing, great especially as a midday pick-me-up
* Perks up skin - adds hydration, doesn't make skin look oily or greasy
* Surprisingly more compact than it looks (but see below)
* The white packaging & shape help it stand out from my other products & from the other Rhode skincare products
* Adds a soft glow
* Can be used to help give a little more slip to thicker makeup products (concealer, etc.), which helps them blend easier
* Good year round
* Great hydrating ingredients

AREA(S) FOR IMPROVEMENT:
* Would love to be able to see how much product remains/has been used
* Being nit picky here, the cap, while cute, could be less bulky

FYI:
* Remember to shake before use
* Gives a soft glow (I don’t personally get a “next level glow” as claimed; it’s a more of a brightened, illuminated complexion)
* Fragrance free (and unscented)
* Can be used on the body as well (but I have not yet tried that)
* Price-wise, there are more budget-friendly mists available (and more expensive ones, for that matter). I've not tried ones comparable to Rhode and cannot make a direct comparison. 

BUY, BUY, BUY 🛍️ or BYE-BYE 👋🏼?
* I have a handful of mists in my rotation and am not in need of another one, but based solely on performance, I would (and have) repurchased another one of these from Rhode. BUY 🛍️

Author: itsfi
Title: Performance 5 ⭐️; scent strength/longevity 3.5 ⭐️
ReviewText:
I’ve used this hand sanitizer at least once a day (usually more) for the past week and a half. 

WHAT I LIKE:
* Touchland hand sanitizers generally leave my hands clean and hydrated without feeling  sticky or greasy. That remained the case with this Gingerbread scented hand sanitizer.
* Soft, not overwhelming gourmand scent with a holiday feel to it - subtle mix of sweet & spicy with its gingerbread, cinnamon & vanilla notes (but see below) 
* Good & practical design - sleek, lightweight & portable, fits easily in purse or pocket, travel friendly, doesn't leak
* The mist that is dispensed with each spritz is nice - not too overpowering.
* Absorbs/dries quickly
* No sticky, tacky or filmy residue

AREA(S) FOR IMPROVEMENT:
* With some of the newer, limited edition scents, I've noticed more of an alcohol smell with the first half dozen or so sprays. Not sure why this is the case as I've never had this issue with the permanent scents. 
* Would be great if these were refillable (without compromising how well the design keeps product from leaking).
* To my nose, this is a very soft, fleeting scent; I wouldn't mind if all the notes were stronger.
* The scent on this doesn't last as long as the permanent scents or the other limited edition ones. Would like to have the scent linger longer. 

FYI:
* Limited edition seasonal scent. New scent for 2025. Once it's sold out, that'll be it, until next year if they bring it back.
* This scent can be purchased individually or as part of a trio of limited edition seasonal scents that includes spiced pumpkin-tini & peppermint mocha - the set does not include the salted caramel scent. 
* Makes a nice gift.

BUY, BUY, BUY 🛍️ or BYE-BYE 👋🏼?:
* While this Gingerbread isn't my favorite scent among the limited edition seasonal collection, I like it enough to pick up another of these if I finish it before the end of the year (and if it's still around). It’s also one I would purchase as a gift for others. BUY 🛍️

Don’t waste your money because the clock app aesthetic influencers have you thinking you need this. In fact, if you are in the US, five below the discount store, has a dupe. I actually bought some of those to compare. The packaging is the same, the container is the same shape, and there are some fun scents. My favorite is the pineapple. Author: kmb7800
Title: Touchland Rainwater Scent
ReviewText:
This sanitizer is good value, even though it looks bit fancier and is more expensive than the typical drugstore hand sanitizer.  One spray bottle lasts a while, although a spritz or two isn’t enough to cover a pair of hands.  Personally, I need at least 4 spritzes per application.  Even so, it still lasts a good number of weeks, depending on usage.

The Rainwater scent is fresh but can be overpowering.  Coming from using alcohol sprays with the smell dissipating after a while, the Touchland sanitizer smell seems to last hours.  It may or not may not be a good thing, depending on how one handles scents.  As far as effectivity is concerned, the back of the case indicates that its active ingredient is “Alcohol 70% v/v”, which is usual for commercial hand sanitizers.

The best thing about the sanitizer though is its packaging.  It’s easy to stash, not just because of its size, but because of its shape.  Because it’s angular and not circular like most spray bottles, it’s easier to find space for it and tuck it in corners, or even pockets.  

Would definitely purchase again but perhaps will try the unscented version next time.

Author: BriTucson
Title: Unimpressed
ReviewText:
Hi. I only write reviews if something is exceptionally good or exceptionally bad. This product, by and large, is the latter, unfortunately. 

I don't know how this has so many good reviews (I guess if you filter by non-incentivized and verified purchase, there aren't, but that's my mistake).

The one good thing about this product seems to be that it isn't drying. I wouldn't call it "hydrating"; any product with alcohol likely won't be. 

I've tried four (4) scents and the only one I like is the salted caramel. It's very strong, but I think it is warm and caramelly-smelling. That being said, my husband hates it and says it smells like cotton candy.

The vanilla blossom literally smells like OFF! (the insect repellent). I used dish soap to get the scent off because it was offensively bad. 

The beach coco smells like chemical coconut. It smells like coconut, if coconut were made in a laboratory, alongside sugar alcohols.

Had high hopes for the spiced pumpkin-tini, which when dry only smells like mild cinnamon. It's not bad, but it'd be more accurate to just call it "cinnamon". 

Quite bold of this brand to charge $10 a bottle for this quality. I don't know if I'll bother to return it and may just give it away. Won't be repurchasing.
